literal: Clear in mind and few in desires; officials and commoners were settled under him.
idiomatic: Clear-minded and few in desires, officials and people were at ease under him.

literal: Xianwen edicted that overseer officials who took one sheep or one hu of wine from those they oversaw would be guilty up to capital punishment;
idiomatic: Xianwen edicted: overseers who took one sheep or one hu of wine from those they oversaw faced capital punishment;

literal: those who gave would be judged as accomplices by association.
idiomatic: those who gave were judged accomplices.

literal: Those who exposed guilt among the Masters of Writing and below would each receive appointment according to the weight of the official they exposed.
idiomatic: Whoever exposed guilt among officials to Masters of Writing and below would be appointed according to the rank of the man exposed.

literal: Baize memorialized, thinking that if this law were carried on without end, he feared treacherous men would spy and diligent ministers would slacken their integrity; he asked to follow the statutes' old law.
idiomatic: Baize memorialized: carry this law on forever and treacherous men will watch while diligent ministers slacken. Follow the old statutes.

literal: Xianwen accepted it.
idiomatic: Xianwen accepted it.

literal: In Taihe's early years more than thirty men of Huai commandery, Yi Qi Gou and others, plotted rebellion; Empress Dowager Wencheng wished to execute the whole city's people.
idiomatic: In early Taihe more than thirty men of Huai, Yi Qi Gou and others, plotted rebellion. Empress Dowager Wencheng wished to kill the whole city.

literal: Baize remonstrated, holding that in the Documents of Zhou the crimes of father, son, and brothers do not reach one another, that one does not falsely implicate ten households—how much less a whole commandery.
idiomatic: Baize remonstrated: the Documents of Zhou do not link father, son, and brother in guilt. Do not implicate ten houses—how much less a commandery.

literal: The empress later followed him and stopped.
idiomatic: The empress later followed him and stopped.

literal: He was transferred to Regular Attendant and Attendant of the Palace Masters of Writing.
idiomatic: He was made Regular Attendant and Attendant of the Palace Masters of Writing.

literal: At death he was posthumously made Inspector of Xiangzhou and Duke of Guangping, posthumous name Jian.
idiomatic: He died. Posthumously Inspector of Xiangzhou and Duke of Guangping, posthumous name Jian.

literal: His eldest son Lun, styled Tiannian, was Vice Minister of the Grand Granary and Rectifier of Yan.
idiomatic: Eldest son Lun, styled Tiannian, was Vice Minister of the Grand Granary and Rectifier of Yan.

literal: In Xiping, the Rouran lord Chounu sent envoys to court, using the ritual of a rival state and not observing minister's respect.
idiomatic: In Xiping the Rouran lord Chounu sent envoys using rival-state ritual, without minister's courtesy.

literal: Court discussion wished to follow Han's precedent in answering the Xiongnu and send envoys in reply.
idiomatic: Court wished to follow Han's answer to the Xiongnu and send envoys in reply.

literal: Lun memorialized, holding: "Though the barbarians admire virtue, they also come to observe us.
idiomatic: Lun memorialized: "Though the barbarians admire virtue, they also come to observe us.

literal: If we awe them with strength, perhaps they will submit;
idiomatic: Awe them with strength and perhaps they submit;

literal: if we show them weakness, covetous watching may arise.
idiomatic: show weakness and covetous eyes may open.

literal: What the Spring and Autumn calls 'they take us as their oracle.'"
idiomatic: The Spring and Autumn says: they take us as their oracle."

literal: Gaozu and Shizong knew this: when they came, none went against them; when they left, none pursued.
idiomatic: Gaozu and Shizong knew this: when they came, none opposed; when they left, none pursued.

literal: Only when they came with tribute of jade and silks and bent knee in vassal ritual did they heap rewards and lend precious things.
idiomatic: Only when they came with jade and silk and bent the knee in vassal ritual did the court heap rewards and lend treasures.

literal: But when royal envoys went far on mission to the barbarian court, honored with rival dignity and given longing favor, I fear it would only breed barbarian insolence and benefit the holy court little."
idiomatic: Send royal envoys far into the barbarian court, honor them as equals, add longing favor—I fear only barbarian insolence, little gain for the holy court."

literal: " They did not follow him.
idiomatic: " They did not listen.

literal: In early Xiaozhuang he died as Minister of the Grand Granary.
idiomatic: In early Xiaozhuang he died as Minister of the Grand Granary.

literal: Gun's younger brother Xun.
idiomatic: Gun's younger brother Xun.

literal: Xun, styled Hongrang, followed his elder brother Gun north and participated in the Prince of Dai's military affairs.
idiomatic: Xun, styled Hongrang, followed Gun north and joined the Prince of Dai's military affairs.

literal: He advised Daowu that he ought to win the hopes of the gentry and commoners of the central lands to establish great enterprise.
idiomatic: He advised Daowu to win the hopes of central gentry and people to build great enterprise.

literal: The emperor greatly valued and distinguished him.
idiomatic: The emperor greatly valued him.

literal: In Huangshi's early years he was appointed Central Secretariat Gentleman.
idiomatic: In early Huangshi he was Central Secretariat Gentleman.

literal: In curtain stratagems he also participated.
idiomatic: He also joined secret stratagems.

literal: He was enfeoffed Viscount of Pinggao and went out as Governor of Guangping.
idiomatic: He was enfeoffed Viscount of Pinggao and went out as Governor of Guangping.

literal: Xun gathered the scattered and urged farming and sericulture; refugees who returned numbered several thousand households.
idiomatic: Xun gathered the scattered, urged farming and sericulture. Thousands of refugee households returned.

literal: He was transferred to Governor of Changshan.
idiomatic: He was transferred to Governor of Changshan.

literal: Xun founded schools and honored scholars with courtesy; officials and people sang of him.
idiomatic: Xun founded schools and honored scholars. Officials and people sang of him.

literal: In the time after chaos, few could be strict with themselves; only Xun in office was pure and white, benevolent and forgiving to those below—the common people loved him, and his government was first in the age.
idiomatic: After chaos few were strict. Only Xun in office was pure, benevolent below—the people loved him. His government was first in the age.

literal: When Mingyuan acceded, he was summoned as Grand Master of the Palace.
idiomatic: When Mingyuan acceded he was summoned Grand Master of the Palace.

literal: He died.
idiomatic: He died.

literal: Xun by nature was pure and frugal; on the day of his death his household had no surplus wealth.
idiomatic: Xun was pure and frugal. On the day he died his house had no surplus.

literal: Posthumously made Inspector of Bingzhou and Marquis of Pinggao, posthumous name Xuan.
idiomatic: Posthumously Inspector of Bingzhou and Marquis of Pinggao, posthumous name Xuan.

literal: His son Chun, styled Daoshang, inherited the title.
idiomatic: Son Chun, styled Daoshang, inherited.

literal: Because of an offense he was stripped.
idiomatic: Stripped for an offense.

literal: Chun's younger brother Dai, styled Dingyan, was Governor of Chenliu and Pingbei.
idiomatic: Brother Dai, styled Dingyan, was Governor of Chenliu and Pingbei.

literal: At death he was posthumously made Inspector of Yingzhou, posthumous name Marquis Hui.
idiomatic: He died. Posthumously Inspector of Yingzhou, posthumous name Marquis Hui.

literal: Where Dai held office he was praised; he had his father's surviving style.
idiomatic: Where Dai served he was praised. He had his father's style.

literal: Dai's son Changnian was Governor of Runan.
idiomatic: Dai's son Changnian was Governor of Runan.

literal: Brothers Liu Chongzhi of the commandery divided their property; the household was poor and had only one ox, which they disputed and could not settle, suing in the commandery court.
idiomatic: Brothers Liu Chongzhi divided property. Poor, with one ox, they disputed and sued at the commandery court.

literal: Changnian, grieved, saw them and said: "You quarrel because you have one ox;
idiomatic: Changnian saw them in grief and said: "You quarrel because you have one ox;

literal: if you had two oxen, you would surely not dispute."
idiomatic: had you two, you would not dispute."

literal: He therefore gave them one ox of his own.
idiomatic: He gave them one of his own oxen.

literal: Thereupon within the district each warned the other and all became respectful and yielding.
idiomatic: Within the district each warned the other. All became respectful and yielding.

literal: He died in the commandery.
idiomatic: He died in office.

literal: His son Chen, styled Baogui, in youth had filial conduct and reached the post of Colonel of the Crown Prince's Supporting Army.
idiomatic: Son Chen, styled Baogui, had filial conduct in youth and reached Colonel of the Crown Prince's Supporting Army.

literal: He died.
idiomatic: He died.

literal: Deng Yanhai was a man of Anding.
idiomatic: Deng Yanhai was from Anding.

literal: His grandfather Qiang was General of Chariots and Cavalry under Fu Jian.
idiomatic: Grandfather Qiang was Chariots and Cavalry General under Fu Jian.

literal: His father Yi was Chancellor of Hejian.
idiomatic: Father Yi was Chancellor of Hejian.

literal: When Murong Chui besieged Ye, Yi was made Inspector of Ji and Marquis of Zhending.
idiomatic: When Murong Chui besieged Ye, Yi was made Inspector of Ji and Marquis of Zhending.

literal: He refused the envoy, saying: "My late father was loyal to the house of Qin; how can Yi go over to the enemy first?"
idiomatic: He refused the envoy: "My father was loyal to Qin. How can Yi betray first?"

literal: A loyal minister does not serve two masters; I dare not hear the command."
idiomatic: A loyal minister does not serve two masters. I dare not obey."

literal: Chui sent someone to persuade him: "I and the Chariots and Cavalry General became sworn brothers of different surnames; you are also like my son and younger brother—how can you decline?"
idiomatic: Chui persuaded him: "Your grandfather and I were sworn brothers. You are as my son—how can you refuse?"

literal: " Yi said: "Ji ought to be entrusted to kin and worthies; Yi asks for another service to offer his life."
idiomatic: " Yi said: "Ji should go to kin and worthies. Give Yi another post to die in."

literal: " Chui therefore employed him as Governor of Hejian.
idiomatic: " Chui made him Governor of Hejian.

literal: Later he died as Internal Governor of Zhao commandery.
idiomatic: Later he died as Internal Governor of Zhao commandery.

literal: Yanhai by nature was pure and plain; words and conduct could be retraced; he broadly read the classics and was skilled in Yi divination.
idiomatic: Yanhai was pure and plain, his words traceable. He read the classics broadly and excelled in Yi divination.

literal: When Daowu pacified the central plains, Yanhai was promoted to Compiler and twice transferred to Gentleman of the Ministry of Personnel.
idiomatic: When Daowu pacified the central plains Yanhai was Compiler, then twice Gentleman of the Ministry of Personnel.

literal: Yanhai clearly understood institutions, knew many precedents, and with Minister Cui Hong fixed court ritual, statutes, music, and military and state documents and edicts—many were Yanhai's work.
idiomatic: Yanhai knew institutions and precedents. With Cui Hong he fixed court ritual, law, music, and state documents—much was Yanhai's.

literal: He was granted the title Viscount of Xiabo.
idiomatic: He was granted Viscount of Xiabo.

literal: Daowu edicted Yanhai to compile a National Record of more than ten scrolls, only arranging year and month and daily conduct, without yet a form and example.
idiomatic: Daowu ordered Yanhai to compile a National Record of more than ten scrolls—only year, month, and daily acts, without form.

literal: Yanhai was careful in court affairs and never went against the intent.
idiomatic: Yanhai was careful at court and never went against intent.

literal: His younger cousin by the father's line Hui was then Gentleman of the Masters of Writing, fierce and knight-errant, curious by nature, and thick with Marquis of Dingling He Ba.
idiomatic: His cousin Hui was then Gentleman of the Masters of Writing—fierce, curious, thick with Marquis of Dingling He Ba.

literal: Ba had a crime and was executed; his sons and younger brothers fled to Chang'an.
idiomatic: Ba was executed for a crime. His sons and brothers fled to Chang'an.

literal: Someone reported that Hui would send them out; because of this Daowu suspected he knew and therefore granted Yanhai death.
idiomatic: Someone reported Hui would send them out. Daowu suspected knowledge and granted Yanhai death.

literal: Afterward he repented of it.
idiomatic: Afterward he repented.

literal: Men of the time all pitied and mourned him.
idiomatic: All pitied him.

literal: His son Ying inherited the title and was gradually promoted to Central Secretariat Gentleman.
idiomatic: Son Ying inherited and rose to Central Secretariat Gentleman.

literal: Taiwu edicted Minister of Ceremonies Cui Hao to gather literary men to compile the National Record; Ying with Hao's brother Lan and others all participated in the compilation.
idiomatic: Taiwu ordered Cui Hao to gather scholars for the National Record. Ying joined with Hao's brother Lan and others.

literal: Taiwu favored the southern desert; the Gaoche Mo Fu Ku Yu Gan led several tens of thousands of horsemen driving more than a million deer to the imperial camp.
idiomatic: Taiwu favored the southern desert. Gaoche Mo Fu Ku Yu Gan led tens of thousands of horse, driving more than a million deer to the camp.

literal: An edict ordered Ying to compose the text and inscribe it on the southern desert to record merit.
idiomatic: Ying was ordered to write the text and inscribe it on the southern desert to record merit.

literal: Concurrently Regular Attendant, envoy to Song.
idiomatic: Also Regular Attendant, envoy to Song.

literal: Advanced to marquis.
idiomatic: Advanced to marquis.

literal: At death posthumous name Marquis Wengong.
idiomatic: He died. Posthumous name Marquis Wengong.

literal: His son Yi inherited the title, held the post of Inspector of Jing, and was granted Duke of Nanyang.
idiomatic: Son Yi inherited, was Inspector of Jing, Duke of Nanyang.

literal: He died.
idiomatic: He died.

literal: His son Shi; Xiaowen granted the name Shu and he held the post of Inspector of Qi.
idiomatic: Son Shi. Xiaowen granted the name Shu. He was Inspector of Qi.

literal: At the first reorganization of the hundred offices, the chief aide to the grand tutor was newly prized; Shu was made Chief Clerk to Grand Tutor Yuan Pi.
idiomatic: At the first reorganization of offices the grand tutor's chief aide was prized anew. Shu was Chief Clerk to Grand Tutor Yuan Pi.

literal: He sat as Chief Clerk to the Minister of Works.
idiomatic: He sat as Chief Clerk to the Minister of Works.

literal: Posthumous name Zhen.
idiomatic: Posthumous name Zhen.

literal: Discussion says: In the times of Zhaocheng and Daowu, clouds and thunder were just beginning; as for ordering the realm and weaving custom, men combined civil and martial worth.
idiomatic: The commentators say: In the age of Zhaocheng and Daowu, clouds and thunder were rising. To order the realm and weave custom took men of civil and martial gift together.

literal: Yan Feng was broadly learned and many-hearing; he was first to receive ritual appointment.
idiomatic: Yan Feng was broad in learning and hearing; he was first to receive ritual appointment.

literal: Xu Qian's talent and art were together fine, galloping through hardship and peril.
idiomatic: Xu Qian's talent and craft were fine together, galloping through hardship and peril.

literal: Otherwise, how could imperial enterprise be achieved?
idiomatic: Otherwise how could imperial enterprise stand?

literal: The Cui Hong clan's household was lofty across generations; still amid the founding of power, he bore the weight of the pivot, kept rectitude and completed tasks—rite following the clear temple, as was fitting.
idiomatic: The Cui Hong house was lofty for generations. In the founding hour Hong bore the pivot, kept rectitude and finished the work—rites for the clear temple, as was fitting.

literal: Hao's arts and learning penetrated broadly; he thoroughly viewed astronomy; in governing affairs and stratagem, none of the time was second to him.
idiomatic: Hao's arts ran broad; he mastered astronomy; in counsel and statecraft none stood second.

literal: This is why he compared himself to Zifang.
idiomatic: This is why he likened himself to Zifang.

literal: In the autumn of Mingyuan's government and the days of Taiwu's campaigning, his words were heard and plans followed; he tranquilly swept the central land; the favor shown was already deep, the diligence already luxuriant.
idiomatic: In Mingyuan's autumn and Taiwu's campaigning days his words were heard and plans obeyed. He swept the central land. Favor was deep; diligence was rich.

literal: Though stratagem covered the age, his awe had not shaken the ruler; at the end of the road chance struck, and he could not preserve himself.
idiomatic: Though stratagem covered the age, his awe never shook the throne. At the road's end chance struck—and he could not save himself.

literal: Was it that when birds are gone the bow is stored, men hate the one above them—or that when the vessel fills it must be leveled, hidden harm brings calamity—why did such a man meet such cruelty?
idiomatic: Was it birds gone, bow stored—men hate the heights? Vessel full, must be leveled—hidden harm brings ruin? Why did such a man meet such cruelty?

literal: As for Zhang Gun's talent and stratagem, he could not escape a harsh end; Yanhai's pure whiteness, disaster not for his crime—pain enough to tell.
idiomatic: Zhang Gun's talent could not escape a harsh end. Yanhai's pure whiteness—disaster not for his crime. Pain enough to tell.

literal: Hongrang was famous through the age as an upright official; his household style is truly worthy to prize.
idiomatic: Hongrang was famed through the age as an upright official. His household style is worth prizing.
